Overview, Historical Timeline, Problems & Solutions You often need to work with words, phrases, or characters in your program. In Python, a string is a sequence of characters. Each character is placed next to the other, in order, inside a pair of quotes. Python lets you use either single quotes or double quotes to mark the start and end of a string. You can think of a string as a row of letter boxes, each holding one character. The first character is at index 0. You can get a letter by its position, or slice a group of letters. Python lets you store and work with text using strings. word = "hello" print(word[0]) # prints h print(word[1:4]) # prints ell
